excerpts.quote: AI is an overused word in this sense. Most of it is just high-end data analytics. Of course, there is some of use of AI, but it is developing. The key, I think, to success, is having the operators partner with the technologists, and they really have to work together. Often the technologists are, you know, we know it all, and other times the operators are, hey, don't bother me with this, I'm busy. Both sides have to accept that partnership. Technologists have to accept the operators' knowledge is essential in developing better data analytics and AI, and the technologists have to work closely, and the operators have to understand the value and the benefit. Part is culture. Every company that is successful at that integration has that partnership.
excerpts.authorship_or_speaker_header: Mr. Feinberg. / next speaker: Senator Ernst.
excerpts.context: Feinberg answers Senator Ernst on AI deployment during his confirmation hearing. This excerpt contains only his uninterrupted answer. His distinction between AI and data analytics qualifies his deployment view.

excerpts.quote: The conflict in Ukraine has demonstrated that the integration of emerging technologies such as drones and artificial intelligence (AI) will shape the future of warfighting and thus are essential tools for preserving the Joint Force's technological advantage over adversaries. I understand that rapid fielding of emerging technologies to enhance the lethality of our warfighters and reestablish deterrence is a key concern for the Secretary of Defense. If confirmed, I will cooperate with stakeholders across the Department to ensure that warfighters can employ emerging technologies such as drones and AI to complement the full array of the Joint Force's capabilities.
excerpts.context: Feinberg answers Senator Cotton, written question 6, on drones and AI in warfare. This is his conditional nomination-stage view. The source does not date this written answer separately.

excerpts.quote: If confirmed, I will work closely with the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security, the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer, the combatant commands, and Military Departments as well as the Deputy Director of National Intelligence, to appropriately prioritize leading-edge AI capabilities that can bring increased lethality or efficiency in operations. We will continue to mature and expand the operationalization of key efforts, such as Project Maven, to improve the accuracy, speed, and precision of intelligence support across the full range of DOD missions.
excerpts.authorship_or_speaker_header: 31. Senator Budd. / Mr. Feinberg. / next question: 32. Senator Budd.
excerpts.context: Feinberg answers Senator Budd, written question 31, on Project Maven and AI intelligence capabilities. The written answer date remains unknown.

excerpts.quote: I will prioritize the Department's efforts to rapidly deliver leading edge AI capabilities at scale, if confirmed. When solutions demonstrate high return on investment in pilots and experiments, it is important to quickly integrate them into both user workflows and the broader architecture. Scalability has historically been a challenge in DOD, but I will focus on creating the right collaborations between industry, users, and program offices to develop and implement transition plans that allow the entire force to effectively scale and sustain the gains leading edge AI can bring to the Department.
excerpts.authorship_or_speaker_header: 32. Senator Budd. / Mr. Feinberg. / next section: Questions Submitted by Senator Eric Schmitt
excerpts.context: Feinberg answers Senator Budd, written question 32, on scaling AI capabilities. The written answer date remains unknown.

excerpts.quote: In addition, I would ensure DOD is fully capitalizing on the benefits of artificial intelligence to advance the Department's priorities, such as the audit.
excerpts.authorship_or_speaker_header: Advance Policy Questions appendix; answer on modern management tools and systems.
excerpts.context: An answer in Feinberg’s appended advance-policy questionnaire discusses digital transformation and financial audit. It is his answer, not the committee question. The written answer date remains unknown.
excerpts.question_anchor: If confirmed, how would you ensure a broader use of modern management tools and systems that you would seek to implement at the Department of Defense, if confirmed?
excerpts.next_question_anchor: The Department of Defense is one of the most complex organizations in the Federal Government.

excerpts.quote: The United States is confronting an increasingly complex national security threat environment. As our adversaries pursue military modernization, developments in artificial intelligence (AI), biotechnology, quantum sciences, microelectronics, space, cyber, and unmanned systems are rapidly transforming the nature of conflict and the global threat landscape.
excerpts.authorship_or_speaker_header: STATEMENT BY DIRECTOR, DEFENSE INTELLIGENCE AGENCY LT. GEN. JAMES ADAMS, USMC
excerpts.context: Adams’s prepared testimony, national-security threat section. The committee’s dated hearing page directly links this document under his full name. His assessment concerns military threats, not a blanket judgment about AI.

excerpts.quote: AI almost certainly will be the most influential technology for future warfare because it has the potential to enhance every aspect of military power, including C4ISR, electronic warfare, autonomous robotic system and swarm operations, logistics, and equipment design.
excerpts.authorship_or_speaker_header: STATEMENT BY DIRECTOR, DEFENSE INTELLIGENCE AGENCY LT. GEN. JAMES ADAMS, USMC
excerpts.context: Adams’s prepared testimony, emerging-technology section on page 30. This forecasts military utility; it does not by itself establish an overall social stance. The dated committee page directly links this testimony.

excerpts.quote: Through artificial intelligence, advanced analytics and open source analysis, DIA is already accelerating our ability to generate new insights.
excerpts.authorship_or_speaker_header: Adams, speaking at Friday’s ceremony, said the agency needs to transform.
excerpts.context: A direct quotation from Adams at his assumption-of-directorship ceremony. In the surrounding answer he emphasizes the continued need for professional judgment and tradecraft. The reporter distinguishes Adams’s words from Hansell’s preceding remarks.

excerpts.quote: We're applying new technology to help us reconcile data, right? Generative AI is a game changer for that. The Marine Corps passed their audit through brute force. They get a lot of people to look at Excel sheets and reconcile data. We can do that with technology now. And so, it's really changing how we approach the audit and our likelihood of achieving one within this administration.
excerpts.context: Hurst answers an audit question during the FY2027 budget briefing. The source names Jules “Jay” Hurst and labels this uninterrupted answer MR. HURST. Financial audits are not embedded AI auditors.

excerpts.quote: There is also a presidential priorities category in our budget, and that includes investments in Golden Dome, drone dominance, AI and data infrastructure, and, critically, the defense industrial base.
excerpts.context: Hurst’s opening budget presentation identifies AI infrastructure among presidential spending priorities. This is a funding description, not a position on a named AI bill.

excerpts.quote: AI/ML technologies offer defense leaders incredible tools to attack longstanding problems, but they are not solutions in and of themselves.
excerpts.context: Hurst’s authored essay advises defense leaders to assess costs, feasibility and alternatives before AI adoption. The author disclaimer expressly separates his views from government policy. Historical date retained.

excerpts.quote: Our job is to embrace the ongoing technological revolution and harness it as a strategic advantage and not a threat
excerpts.authorship_or_speaker_header: Dustin Gard-Weiss, deputy director of national intelligence for policy and capabilities, ODNI
excerpts.context: Gard-Weiss’s keynote addresses emerging technologies, including AI, communications, biotechnology and materials. This quote describes a strategic mission. It does not isolate AI or establish that all AI effects are beneficial. Historical date retained.
